- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% relative to prior 30d mean.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30d horizon (first 5–7 days) after a spike or correction; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- After a sharp price drop (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a 1–3% upward bias to forecast 10–15 days ahead to counteract underestimation.
- If sentiment history shows multiple consecutive 0.00 values, model exhibits high volatility bias; apply a 1–2% smoothing filter to forecast slope to reduce overreaction.
- When true outcome shows a sustained downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 55), model tends to underestimate; apply a 2–4% upward bias to forecast 10–20 days ahead to capture mean reversion.
- If sentiment history includes 0.20 or higher, model often overreacts to short-term noise; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast 5–10 days ahead to dampen overoptimism.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcomes in the final 5–7 days of 30d horizon; apply a 1–3% upward bias to last 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
